questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I always knew I wanted to go on exchange and had always thought I'd go to the US, but upon browsing through the partner agreements my home university had, I realized that I had never considered going to Asia and thought that was a shame as I perceive Asia to be "the future" with the changing world order etc. I choose Singapore as it works as a great bridge between the west and the east, and to this end thought there were great benefits to the main language being English.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was an administrative downside as I had to learn the system at NUS, but once I was able to look past all the different platforms and the overload of information, I really did feel that "my hand was held" the entire time upon arrival in terms of what I needed to get done/when to get it done/where to get it done. I suggest taking notes of what needs to be done though, because otherwise it really feels like information overload.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A lot of the assistance and information was online even when getting to my accommodation all I needed to do was download an app that worked as the key to my dorm.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: NUS offers a big range of campus housing options. I stayed at Sheares Hall, which is more similar to a classic dorm and was mostly filled with locals. It was very social, but mostly for locals, but in that sense it is a great opportunity if you want to 'integrate' and get to know Singapore from an insider perspective. However, the downside with staying at the hall was that it was an older building without AC, which trust me means a lot in Singapore. If I could I would've stayed at a UTown Residence or anything else at UTown or PGP, my impression is also that the other exchange students had an easier time participating in social events etc. as those were happening at their accommodation.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Breakfast and dinner was part of the rent paid. It is a good deal, but for someone who's a foodie I opted for eating out mostly. If you want to save money it is great, but the quality of the food is not amazing and that is a shame when in Singapore as you're immersed with lots of different and delicious food.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Try to get accommodation in PGP or anything at UTown! The halls have more of an authentic feel as it is filled with locals, but I honestly think it is okay to be in an 'exchange bubble' if it means doing more social things and having a room with AC/better facilities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The downside was really the lack of AC, having to share not-so-great bathrooms and showers with about 15 other women that got dirty super easily. In the other accommodations you share with less people (about 4 or so), and as the other people at the hall had already been living together and gotten to know each other in the first sem, I think you're easily overlooked as an exchanger whereas the other places are more packed with exchangers and are thus more social.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: So many different platforms throughout different stages of the process. I think NUS should streamline their platforms a little more.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I was given a flowchart, but it was very administrative heavy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They did offer lots of services on campus!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted!

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take notes of what you need to do/look at the flowchart, it is easy to overlook something also in terms of finishing the VISA process in person.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It is a different kind of law you learn. It is more doctrinal, which I think could have a lot to do with the differences between a civil law system and a common law one.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Depends a bit on the class, but I felt that participation was more normalized at NUS. The professors are very interested in hearing what you have to say/what options you hold, which was very refreshing and a lot more engaging.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Law and Democracy in East Asia 
Current Problems in International Law 
Human Rights in Asia 
Traditional Chinese Legal Thought

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would honestly take a look at who's teaching the different courses and choose professors that are well-known/pioneers within their respective fields. I by chance ended up taking a class with Antony Anghie who's a great legal thinker within a specific school of international law, and that has hands-down been one of the highlights of my academic time - to be taught by someone to talented.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I by accident went to the doctor outside of NUS health clinic which was a huge mistake as I had to pay lot, which my insurance at the time didn't cover.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out (especially at hawker centers) and transportation was less expensive than I thought, but groceries were quite expensive!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had everything from barista clubs, astronomy club, student podcasts, different festivals etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sailing club or the outdoor adventure club!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel, travel, travel! You can take a bus to Kuala Lumpur, JB or take relatively cheap flights to other Asian countries! I went to Malaysia (Langkawi and Kuala Lumpur), Thailand, Hong Kong, Taiwan, South Korea, Japan, Vietnam and Indonesia (Bali). If you know you want to travel upon the end of the semester or throughout during the different holidays, I recommend saving some money before heading on exchange.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Super easy as it is quite westernized.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to people in class!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Maybe the fact that freedom of speech is less free.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The politeness, diversity, respect and food culture!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find a way to strike the balance between academia and all the social and cultural opportunities you're going to have while on exchange. It is an amazing opportunity to learn things/courses you cannot otherwise learn back home (also seeing that Asia is a huge growing economy it is super useful to learn about from the inside), but at the same time there are also other important things about about on exchange in terms of personal growth and experiences.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a larger emphasis on participation which might seem intimidating at first, but my experience is that whereas back home there is often a 'right or wrong' answer here it is more the professors looking for you to engage with them and share your opinions

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The connection I now feel to Singapore and all the places I got to travel to.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not having more time. Time flew by and as I was really getting settled into everyday life and started knowing the city well/having favorite places throughout, I had to go back ):

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It is hands down one of the best things I've ever done in my life.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
